subject: Urgent MAP checkpoint request — executive sponsor & SLA escalation
messages:
From: Elena Voss <elena.voss@northbridgecap.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Tan <michael.tan@northbridgecap.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: UAT SLA incidents — request MAP checkpoint and exec sponsor involvement

Sean,

We surfaced repeated SLA violations in our UAT cluster yesterday and this morning that are blocking our performance evaluation. P95 latency spikes to ~4.2s on short prompts, and several token-generation failures returned 502s. I've attached an incident log (incident_log_20260301.csv) with timestamps and example request IDs.

Given the impact on our evaluation timeline (we are aiming to close pilot by 2026-03-15), we need an immediate MAP checkpoint with executive sponsor involvement. Specifically:
- Confirm priority support / SLA exception to accelerate triage
- Propose fix window and mitigation plan that keeps our evaluation on schedule
- Update MAP with action items and owners so our procurement/legal teams can see an approvable path to production

Can you please schedule a brief checkpoint and escalate to your support lead? Time is sensitive — Michael and I are available Mon/Wed afternoons PT.

Thanks,
Elena Voss
Head of ML Engineering
NorthBridge Capital

Attachment: incident_log_20260301.csv (CSV, 32KB)

Proposed immediate steps:
- I’ll get a priority support ticket opened right now and request SLA exception for triage (SE will add logs and repro).
- Can we schedule a 30-min MAP checkpoint tomorrow (Mon 2026-03-02) at 2:00pm PT? If that doesn't work, Wed 3rd at 3:00pm PT.
- We will produce an updated MAP PDF with action items and owners after the call and share it with your procurement/legal teams.

I’m attaching our working MAP (NB_MAP_v2.pdf) and will confirm the support case number once Jasmine creates it.

—Sean

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Notes: MAP checkpoint (2026-03-03) — summary & action items

Team,

Thanks for joining the MAP checkpoint earlier today. Below is a concise record of what we covered and the agreed next steps. I’m keeping these intentionally pragmatic so your procurement/legal teams can rely on them for timeline commitments.

Meeting summary:
- Incident recap: multiple short-prompt P95 spikes and intermittent 502s during UAT window (see incident_log).
- Root-cause hypothesis: network-level retransmissions + intermittent KV-cache invalidation on a small subset of model shards under UAT load pattern.
- Immediate mitigation: temporary routing to a warmed variant (quantized v1.3-warm) to reduce cold-start overheads.
- Longer-term: back-end patch to KV cache consistency (estimated 48–72 hours plus testing).

Action items (owner — due):
1) Jasmine Liu — create priority support ticket, upload debug dump, and request SLA exception (SUP-4521) — due 2026-03-03 17:00 PT.
2) Mateo Alvarez — review backend patch and allocate a dev to build test branch; propose small-change CR and target hotfix window — due 2026-03-04 12:00 PT.
3) Marissa Cole — update MAP PDF with items & send to procurement/legal (NB_MAP_v2 -> NB_MAP_v3) — due 2026-03-04 18:00 PT.
4) Sean Gallagher — coordinate exec sponsor update and confirm support credits/compensation conversation with leadership — due 2026-03-05 EOD PT.
5) Elena / NorthBridge — provide a prioritized list of eval prompt sets and critical SLA targets (P50/P95 goals) — due 2026-03-04 12:00 PT.

Attachments distributed: NB_MAP_v2.pdf (working map), support_dump_0303.zip (SE debug dump).

I will circulate NB_MAP_v3 once Marissa finishes edits. If we need an executive touchpoint before the hotfix, Sean will escalate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks for the clear triage notes and the dump. I’ve reviewed the traces and we have a plausible patch that addresses KV cache eviction race under parallel warm-up. I’m assigning Miguel from backend to produce a test branch today. Proposed remediation plan:

- 2026-03-05: patch branch + CI run (Miguel)
- 2026-03-06: canary deployment to warmed variant, smoke test against NorthBridge’s load profile
- 2026-03-07: if canary stable, schedule hotfix window in low-traffic hours (we will reserve 2x burst capacity and coordinate with operations)

I’ve also approved an SLA exception for triage + overnight hotfix candidate evaluation. I’m attaching a short change request doc for audit (change_request_NB-4521.pdf).

Support ticket SUP-4521 is now flagged as priority in our system. I’ll update the ticket with CI logs and will ping operations to reserve the burst capacity for the hotfix.

- Sean will confirm any operational credits and formal SLA exceptions with leadership by 2026-03-09 EOD PT.

- Please share your priority prompt set and P50/P95 thresholds by 2026-03-04 so we can validate against the canary tests and updated MAP.
- If you want a short exec touchpoint with Ava and me, we can schedule 15 minutes this week; otherwise we’ll send a final status note after hotfix verification.

We understand the evaluation timeline pressure and are treating this as a high-priority remediation path. I’ll follow up in HubSpot and update SUP-4521 with progress notes.
